_comment: Approximate geographic centroids for ISO 3166-2:IN subdivisions, plus a
Static and bundled on purpose. The velocity signal needs a distance between
two coarse places; it does not need a street, and a request-time call to a
geo service would put a third-party outage inside a public endpoint and put
a scanner's IP address in somebody else's log.
Degrees, WGS84, one decimal of real precision. These are state centroids,
so a distance computed from them is accurate to a few hundred kilometres --
which is the right resolution for a threshold set at 900 km/h and the wrong
resolution for anything that looks like tracking a person.
Both IN-OD and the retired IN-OR are present, and both IN-UK and the retired
IN-UT, because real request headers still carry the old codes.
